entries.subject: probe-texts: report who the FUB API key actually is
entries.title: probe-texts: report who the FUB API key actually is
entries.body:
The first pass answered the big question — all 17,204 imported texts across 1,003
leads are hidden, none have ever been readable, and showContent / includeContent
change nothing — but it counted rows in /me and /users instead of returning them,
so the most likely cause went unread.

turns on which user the API key belongs to and what that user may see, and that
is the difference between a setting someone can change and a dead end.

Still GET only.

entries.subject: Read-only probes: why an imported FUB text says the body is hidden
entries.title: Read-only probes: why an imported FUB text says the body is hidden
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-07: some texts synced from FUB read "* Body is hidden for privacy
reasons *", and he remembers it working before. Mike McMurrin (#46, FUB 39165)
has 57 texts on file and all 57 are hidden — timestamps, direction and both
numbers came through, only the words are missing.

mapText copies t.message verbatim, so that sentence is FUB's, not the Hub's. Two
read-only diagnostics to find out what it depends on:

  GET /api/fub/probe-texts?personId=  asks FUB the same question several ways
      (plain, allFields, showContent, includeContent, single-by-id) and reports
      how many rows came back readable each time, plus /me and the person record
      in case it turns on who owns the lead.

  GET /api/admin/fub-text-privacy     counts hidden vs readable across every
      imported FUB text, by message month, and says whether leads are all-hidden
      or mixed — which separates "this changed recently" from "it was never
      readable for these leads and memory is wrong".

Both are GET only. Nothing is written, nothing is sent.

entries.subject: performance-all selected a column that does not exist
entries.title: performance-all selected a column that does not exist
entries.body:
The endpoint 500'd on its first real call: "no such column: active". I selected
`active` from drip_campaigns, but the table has no on/off flag at all — a campaign
runs because something enrolls into it, not because of a flag on the row. I had
assumed the column from a "status=inactive" I saw earlier, which turned out to be
my own throwaway script printing its fallback, not data from the Hub.

Every test passed while this was broken, because they all READ the source. A query
being written is not a query that runs. The new test extracts each SELECT from the
endpoint and executes it against the real schema, and it is verified both ways:
putting `active` back makes it fail with that exact message, taking it out makes
it pass.

Its own extraction bug is worth noting too — the first regex ran past a template
literal's closing backtick into the next query and tested SQL nobody had written.
It now stops at the matching delimiter.

entries.subject: Register /performance-all before the /:id that was swallowing it
entries.title: Register /performance-all before the /:id that was swallowing it
entries.body:
I added the route after router.get('/:id'), so Express matched /performance-all
as id = "performance-all", Number() made it NaN and the lookup 404'd. The symptom
gave nothing away: a poll loop simply never saw the response it was waiting for,
and I spent ten minutes watching an empty file before reading the route order.

Moved above '/:id'. A test now checks the general rule rather than this one case:
no single-segment literal GET route may be registered after a parameter route that
would shadow it, so the next one added is caught too.

Two more tests pin what the endpoint is for: it returns the enrolment and rate
fields, and `since` windows only the email counts. "On a drip right now" is not a
windowed question, and applying the window to both would give a number that means
neither.

and "the last 7 days" and "since the 1st" are different numbers. It echoes the

entries.subject: Group reply box shows the whole message before it sends
entries.title: Group reply box shows the whole message before it sends
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-07: "the group text in Inbox see the message box it does not expand
like the normal text box in 1 on 1 message therefore I can't view the message in
full to review it can you fix the height of that".

The group pane's reply was a single-line <input> while the 1-to-1 pane used a
3-row textarea. A long message - an under-contract note, an inspection window -
scrolled out of sight and could not be read back. A group text goes to several
people at once, which is the worst place to send something unreviewed.

It is a textarea now, opening at the same 3 rows as the 1-to-1 box and growing
with the message up to 40% of the window, then scrolling rather than clipping.
The height resets to auto before each measurement, or the box could only ever get
taller and never shrink back when text is deleted.

Enter still sends, so the shortcut already in people's fingers keeps working, and
Shift+Enter is a new line - the placeholder says so. preventDefault matters there:
without it Enter would send AND leave a newline in the next draft.

resize is off deliberately. The box sizes itself, so a manual drag would be undone
by the next keystroke, which is worse than not offering the handle.

Two details the tests pin: the bar bottom-aligns so the Send button stays beside
the last line instead of towering next to a grown box, and the textarea inherits
the app font so the draft looks like the message that actually goes out.

entries.subject: A group text can no longer report success when it reached nobody
entries.title: A group text can no longer report success when it reached nobody
entries.body:
Matt did not receive the 2026-10-06 congratulations text to Dave and Liz Deutsch. The
live Twilio roster for that conversation held ZERO participants: the message reached
none of the three, the clients included, and the Hub recorded it as sent.

Two things combined.

group_meta - the participant list /group-text matches against when deciding to reuse an
existing conversation - is a snapshot written when the group was created and never
re-read. Twilio allows one binding per phone + proxy pair, so adding any of those phones
to a newer group unbinds it from the older conversation. The snapshot still named all
three; Twilio reached none. Twilio then accepted the message into the empty conversation
and returned a real message SID, which the Hub treated as proof of delivery.

Fixes:
- sendConversationMessage reads the participant list first and throws CONVERSATION_EMPTY
  rather than posting into a conversation that reaches nobody. It returns deliveredTo so
  a caller can no longer mistake a message SID for delivery. This is the single place
  both the group-text reuse path and group-reply go through.
- /group-text confirms the LIVE roster still holds every intended recipient before
  reusing a conversation, and rebuilds the group when it does not. A partial roster
  counts as drifted, since that is the case where one person goes missing unnoticed.

test/group-text-reaches-people.test.mjs covers both halves.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Read-only group roster diagnostic: live Twilio participants vs the Hub's snapshot
entries.title: Read-only group roster diagnostic: live Twilio participants vs the Hub's snapshot
entries.body:
Matt did not receive the 2026-10-06 group text to Dave and Liz Deutsch. The Hub's
group_meta for that conversation lists three participants, but group_meta is a
SNAPSHOT written when the group was created - it is not re-read, and Twilio's live
roster is the only thing that decides who a send actually reaches.

The two can drift by design: createGroupText removes a participant from an older
conversation when their phone + our proxy is already bound elsewhere, because Twilio
allows one binding per phone+proxy pair. So a later group text that included Matt
would have pulled his binding OUT of this conversation, leaving his name in the
thread's history and in group_meta while sends no longer reach him.

GET /api/inbox/group-roster/:convSid reports the live roster, the Hub's snapshot,
and the difference. GETs only - it cannot send anything.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Ramp climbs to the ceiling instead of jumping to it
entries.title: Ramp climbs to the ceiling instead of jumping to it
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-06: "Please increase to 300 a day we need to bump this up and level
up our game".

The warm-up ramp spends five enrolling days at 50 and five at 100, then handed
straight over to the configured ceiling. That was a step of 100 while the ceiling
was 200. With 300 the same code would have gone 100 -> 300 overnight, which is
precisely the shape of volume spike the ramp exists to prevent - and the campaign
has 0 bounces across 311 sends and a 47% open rate, which is worth protecting.

It now keeps climbing a step at a time, never more than +100 in a day, until it
reaches whatever the ceiling is. At 300 that reads 100, 200, 300 rather than
100, 300. A test states the underlying rule: no day more than doubles the one
before it.

The settings response also returns the next few days' limits, because raising the
ceiling while the ramp is still climbing otherwise looks like nothing happened.

11 tests, including that the ramp still counts enrolling days rather than calendar
days, so a weekend or an outage does not spend a step.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Read-only: how a drip campaign is actually performing
entries.title: Read-only: how a drip campaign is actually performing
entries.body:
John asks for the Home Value numbers regularly and the Hub could only answer half
of it: dripStats counts enrollments and successful step executions, but nothing
tied a campaign's sends to their opens.

sendSequenceEmail already stamps email_log.template as `drip_<id>`, and the
SendGrid Event Webhook attaches opens and clicks to those same rows, so
GET /api/drips/:id/performance can count them without guessing from subject lines.

Open rate is of DELIVERED, not of sent - an email that bounced was never a chance
to open, and dividing by sent quietly understates every campaign. Both the
per-email and per-person rates are returned, since one person opening six times
is not six people.

The response says plainly that opens are a floor: a mail client that blocks the
tracking pixel reads the email and never reports it.

entries.subject: Record which number the Hub sent an outgoing text from
entries.title: Record which number the Hub sent an outgoing text from
entries.body:
Checking the new from/to line against the real Misener thread showed every
outgoing message as "? -> (319) 521-6995". from_addr was being stored as '' on
every send, so half of "what number" was missing on our side of every thread the
Hub has ever sent.

sendSms now returns the sending number and the seven 1-to-1 send sites record it.
Twilio's own answer is used first and the configured number is only a fallback,
because with a Messaging Service Twilio picks which number goes out.

Group sends go through a Conversation rather than a plain message, so they keep
no from number; the copy-fallback beside them does, and it reads r2 - the result
its OWN send returned. A blind replace had put r.from there, which would have
been a ReferenceError or, worse, picked up some unrelated r. A test now checks
that each site reads the result its own send returned, looking at the statement
rather than the line, since the insert wraps.

Only new texts carry it. Nothing invents a number for messages already sent.

entries.subject: Every message shows which number it came from and which it went to
entries.title: Every message shows which number it came from and which it went to
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-06, looking at the Jacob Misener thread: "on each text or message
include where the text came from and what number so I know which one texted".

That thread is the case for it. His WIFE replied from his number:

  Jacob Misener · Oct 6, 11:20 AM
  "Hi this is Emily Misener - property owner of 1332 Truman Court NE, the number
   you were texting is my husband so he passed your message onto me."

and two messages later gave her own, 507-251-4908. Every message in it was headed
"Jacob Misener", and the only place a number ever appeared was on a group text, so
nothing on screen said two people and two numbers were involved.

src/components/Endpoints.jsx renders "from -> to" under every text, call,
voicemail and email, in the profile and in all three Inbox panes. One
implementation: the Inbox was formatting a number inline and the profile had its
own copy that only ran when conversation_sid was set.

It also flags a number that is NOT saved on the lead, which is exactly the Emily
case - but only where that can be known. The profile has the full record, so it
passes the client and the flag works. The Inbox does not carry a lead's alt_phones,
so it passes no client and the flag stays off; saying "not on file" about every
message because the caller had nothing to compare would be worse than silence.

A note has no two ends, so it gets nothing.

14 tests, and the helpers are lifted out of the component rather than copied, so
they cannot drift the way a duplicated assessorUrl once did.

entries.subject: Hand-added leads: the exclusion now blocks SENDING, not just enrolment
entries.title: Hand-added leads: the exclusion now blocks SENDING, not just enrolment
entries.body:
John, after the fourth incident here: "I still don't know why you can't simply make
the manual import as exclusion to AI enrollment?"

It WAS one, since 2026-10-02, and that part worked - auto-enrolment refused Megan
Walt and logged it. The hole is that "Send AI now" never asks the enrolment
question: it force-sends. An enrolment-level exclusion is not in its path at all,
which is why guarding enrolment, then campaigns, then status, then two endpoints
each fixed a door and left the room open.

So the flag moved to where messages actually leave. forbidden.js is consulted by
canSendSms on EVERY AI send - scheduled, responsive, forced, bulk, and anything
written later - and it now refuses a lead carrying auto_enroll_excluded.

Saying yes still works and is the only way through: POST /lead/:id/enable clears
the flag (before enabling, or the gate would keep refusing), as does the
Send-AI-now override, both recording who did it.

Proved by unit tests against the real canSendSms, including force:true - the exact
path that texted Megan. Nothing live is called; see the standing rule about never
exercising a send endpoint while investigating.

Blast radius checked first: only 2 leads carry the flag and neither had pending
sends, so nobody's working AI is silently switched off.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: A hand-added lead stays out of the AI until someone says otherwise
entries.title: A hand-added lead stays out of the AI until someone says otherwise
entries.body:
John added Megan Walt by hand at 14:20 and an AI opener went out at 14:27.

The 2026-10-02 guard was NOT at fault and is still working. Her record carried
auto_enroll_excluded=1, stamped by her creator with the right reason, and the
auto-enrolment hook refused her - logged as "status is 'active', only New-status
leads auto-enroll". She had no scheduled AI actions at all.

What got past it was "Send AI now". That endpoint force-sends AND calls
setManaged(true), so one click both sends a message and enrols the lead for good,
while its confirm dialog mentioned neither the exclusion nor the enrolment.

send-now and bulk-send-now now honour the flag: they refuse with needs_override,
BEFORE enrolling or sending. The UI asks a second, explicit question naming the
exclusion and saying plainly that continuing turns AI on for the lead. Clicking
through clears the flag and logs who did it - at that point a person really has
said so, which is all that was asked.

POST /lead/:id/enable is untouched and still does not consult the flag: that
button IS the way to say yes.

entries.subject: An edited note kept its date; the stamp cap was too short
entries.title: An edited note kept its date; the stamp cap was too short
entries.body:
Caught by running the real thing against the live Hub rather than trusting the
tests. Add, the 409 on a stale edit, and delete all behaved, and the 28-line
pasted Zillow block read as one dated note - but the edited note came back with
an EMPTY stamp:

  [] [Oct 6, 2026, 9:44 AM · Hub Automation (edited Oct 6, 2026, 9:44 AM by Hub
  Automation)] round-trip check, edited

The stamp pattern capped at 80 characters, to stop a "[something]" in a note's
body being read as its date. An edited stamp carrying both names is 86. So the
note stopped being recognised as dated, lost its date on screen, and would have
been stamped AGAIN on the next save, burying the real date inside the body - the
exact failure this whole change exists to prevent.

Cap is now 200, past any real stamp and far short of a sentence, in both the
server and the profile parser. The editor is also no longer named when they wrote
the note in the first place, which was most of the extra length and read as
though two people had been involved.

Every test passed while this was broken, because they built stamps shorter than
the cap. The new ones use the exact string the live run produced. 40 tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: A pasted block is one note, not one note plus orphans
entries.title: A pasted block is one note, not one note plus orphans
entries.body:
The audit on the live data said 312 notes across 151 leads, 85 of them undated
across 28 leads. The sample showed what they actually are:

  [10/5/2026] 8/17/2026  Price change
  $339,999
  -2.9%
  $106/sqft
  Source: Owner

One pasted Zillow price history. The old save stamped the first line and left the
rest adrift, so the tail counted as separate undated notes. Stamping those 85
fragments would have put today's date on five-year-old price history and turned
one note into five.

An unstamped line after a note is now the rest of that note. They inherit the real
date of the note they belong to, and the undated count drops to whatever genuinely
starts undated - no invented dates, nothing to backfill.

ensureStamped only stamps a note that STARTS undated, never a continuation.
replaceNote and removeNote act on the note's whole span, so editing a pasted block
replaces all of it instead of orphaning its tail below the new text. The routes
resolve a note through splitNotes and compare `expect` against the whole note;
comparing a single line would let an edit through whenever only the tail changed.

The profile parses identically. If the two disagreed, an edit would target a
different line than the one on screen - which is the whole reason the index comes
from the parse and not from the rendered position. A test pins them together,
including that the stamp is checked before the blank-line skip. 37 tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Notes get an edit button, and every note carries a date
entries.title: Notes get an edit button, and every note carries a date
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-05: "notes in clients profile should have an edit button also make
sure all notes logged in HUB have a date log and moving forward".

clients.notes is one text field, newest first, one note per line. Four code paths
were writing into it and each invented its own stamp:

  ClientProfile.jsx   [Oct 5, 2026, 3:04 PM]       browser local time
  master-file-log.js  [10/5/2026]                   Central, no time
  automations.js      [Oct 5, 2026 - automation]    no time
  lead-intake.js      [2026-10-05]                  and APPENDED, so a brand new
                                                    lead's note read as the oldest
                                                    thing on the file

So whether a note had a date depended on which path wrote it, and the profile
showed one only when the line happened to match its single pattern.

server/client-notes.js now owns the format and all four use it. Times are Central:
a server in UTC stamping a note typed at 8:30pm on Oct 5 would print Oct 6, wrong
on the only thing the stamp is for. The clients PUT route runs ensureStamped over
anything handed to it, so a note cannot land undated whoever writes it - the UI is
not the only writer and a date cannot be recovered after the fact.

An existing stamp is never rewritten. Re-stamping would replace a real date with
today's, which is worse than no date at all.

EDITING. Each note carries the index of its line in the RAW field, so editing the
second search hit rewrites the second match and not the second line on screen -
and blank lines no longer shift what an edit lands on. The request sends back the
line it believed it was editing; if anything changed meanwhile the server answers
409 instead of overwriting it. An edit keeps the original date and records that it
was edited, by whom, once - history is not silently rewritten. Delete is there too,
and the text goes to the activity log so it is recoverable.

Notes with no date at all render "date not recorded" rather than a date nobody
recorded. GET /api/admin/notes-audit counts them and shows a sample; the backfill
decision is John's once the numbers are in. 31 tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Serve the phone SDK from the Hub instead of a CDN
entries.title: Serve the phone SDK from the Hub instead of a CDN
entries.body:
"The Hub phone could not connect: Phone SDK failed to load."

Nothing was wrong with the Hub. jsdelivr was serving the file (200, 301902 bytes)
and the script tag was in the deployed page with no CSP in the way - John's
browser simply could not fetch it within the 9s the widget waits. An ad blocker,
a privacy extension or a VPN exit that filters the request all produce exactly
this, and the message pointed at the Hub instead of at the cause.

The SDK was never an npm dependency, so jsdelivr was its ONLY source. That made
someone else's CDN a single point of failure for the phone: no fallback, no local
copy, and a softphone that stops existing when a third party is unreachable.

The file is now vendored into public/vendor and served from the Hub's own origin,
so anyone who can open the Hub at all can load the phone. jsdelivr stays behind an
onerror as a fallback for the one case a local copy cannot cover - a deploy that
shipped without the vendor file. The tests pin the two ways this silently rots:
the local copy going missing, and the fallback drifting to a different version
than the filename claims.

The error text now names the usual cause instead of only the symptom.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.title: Bring back a dropped message that a kept reply points at
entries.body:

it left an answer with no question: she replied twice to "Market changes for your
home on 7009 Springwood Pl Nw", her replies were kept, and the message she was

entries.subject: Judge an email by the system that generated its Message-ID
entries.title: Judge an email by the system that generated its Message-ID
entries.body:
The live split on Niki Morris's 31 messages failed the real test: 30 kept, 1
dropped, and the six Matrix MLS listing alerts - the exact mail John said to
exclude - were among the kept. Reading subject lines got them wrong six times out
of six, because the alert opens "Dear Niki Morris," and carries a single link, so
every body heuristic read it as a person writing.

Reading the actual headers gave a hard signal instead. From the real mailbox:

  mail.gmail.com     Matt or John typed it in Gmail      a person
  gprodcdra70b       Matrix MLS listing alert            a machine
  followupboss.com   FUB send, X-Mailer PHPMailer        16-38 links, a template
  sierra-vm-srvc3    Sierra drip campaign                a campaign

Matrix and Sierra are alert and campaign engines, so they are never conversation.
FUB is also where an agent types a real reply, so a followupboss.com id drops
only when the body carries a mass template with it - 8+ links or an unsubscribe
footer. A short typed one is kept, because FUB withholds email content from its
own API and Gmail is the only place that copy exists.

A lead's own reply always arrives with a real mail-client Message-ID, so the
reply rule catches it before any of this runs.

9 new tests, each built on a Message-ID read off a real message, including the
two that must survive every rule: "Sample Purchase Agreement" and "Warranty info"
(12 links, all of them images in Matt's signature). 45 tests.

entries.subject: Gmail history import keeps real emails, drops automated listing alerts
entries.title: Gmail history import keeps real emails, drops automated listing alerts
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-05: "we don't need to get automated listing alerts emails only
those actual emails coming from lead or a reply".

The mattsmithremax@gmail.com pull is the route that works - FUB withholds email
content, Gmail does not - but a lead's mailbox history is mostly Ylopo listing
alerts, not conversation. server/email-is-human.js judges each message and the
reason travels with it, so a sample can be reviewed before anything is imported.

Signals, strongest first:
  In-Reply-To / References  -> KEEP, a reply is a conversation by definition
  List-Unsubscribe, List-Id, Auto-Submitted, SendGrid/SES ids -> bulk
  Precedence: bulk/list/junk
  machine local part (no-reply@, alerts@, bounces@)
  platform domains (ylopo, sierrainteractive, kvcore, homebot, fello, ...)
  alert-shaped subject -> only decides when the body ALSO has 4+ links and no
                          greeting; subject alone is never enough

WHEN IN DOUBT, KEEP. A marketing email wrongly kept is clutter; a real
conversation wrongly dropped is history nobody can get back, and having it is
the whole point of the import.

Two traps hit while writing it:
  - the sender pattern matched "updates@" anywhere in a local part, which dropped
    donna.updates@gmail.com, a person. Now anchored on the WHOLE local part, with
    hyphen-joined suffixes (listing-alerts@) still treated as machines and
    dot-separated ones left alone. support@/team@/mail@ are shared mailboxes a
    person writes from, so they are kept.
  - a test sliced importContactHistory with indexOf('return {') and caught the
    early `return { error: 'client not found' }`, so it passed on 200 characters
    of function. Slices now run to the next export - the same bug that once let a
    broken assessor URL stay green.

importContactHistory skips what the classifier rejected and reports
skipped_automated, so a surprising count is visible rather than silent.
include_automated: true on the route overrides it deliberately. 36 tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: AI stops when a lead stops being a prospect, not just when it joins
entries.title: AI stops when a lead stops being a prospect, not just when it joins
entries.body:
Answering John's question honestly: the earlier fix covered the CAMPAIGN fences.
Status was the same bug on a different field and was NOT covered.

"that was hunter's past client so I just moved it to closed, not supposed to get
any AI enrollment." Enrolment only ever takes status='new', but nothing re-read
the status afterwards - so a lead enrolled while New and later moved to Closed
kept its AI. Identical shape to the FSBO case.

forbidden.js now also refuses closed, pending and archived, so it is checked on
every send. junk and donotcontact were already denied upstream by isStopStatus,
and not_in_market by its own proactive rule; these three were catching nothing.

'active' is deliberately NOT included: routes/clients.js defaults a hand-added
lead to 'active', so denying it would quietly switch the AI off for a large and
ordinary part of the base. Asserted.

Scoped to the AI channel, so the Past Client Nurture drip still runs for Closed
leads - also asserted, since silencing that would be a worse bug than the one
being fixed.

Live exposure was one lead, Leo Solamo, already in HUMAN_TAKEOVER with nothing
queued. The 41 junk and 5 not_in_market AI-managed leads carry pending actions but
those were already being denied at send time.

entries.subject: One rule for who the AI may never text, asked again on every send
entries.title: One rule for who the AI may never text, asked again on every send
entries.body:
John: "make sure that nothing of this happens again, also the same problem we had
last time when AI automatically kicked in for a lead that was added manually
which is actually our seller client."

The hand-added case was already fixed on 2026-10-02 (Holly Stock): routes/clients.js
stamps auto_enroll_excluded on the record itself, and enrolment honours it. That
guard is intact and left alone - it stays enrolment-only on purpose, so an agent
switching AI on from the profile still means exactly that.

What was NOT fixed is the shape both incidents share: a fence that only runs when
a lead JOINS. Joseph Green was enrolled as a cold buyer months before anyone knew
he was selling, so the FSBO exclusion never ran again for him.

ai-followup/forbidden.js now holds the campaign-ownership rule in one place -
cx_campaign, fsbo_followups, fb_seller_followups, fsbo_status, fsbo_listings,
mls_status, the FB Seller Ad tag - and policy.js asks it on EVERY send rather than
keeping its own copy. Two copies drift; that is exactly how FSBO came to be
guarded in one place and not the other.

A parity test holds enrolment and send-time together, and it immediately found a
real gap: enrolment fenced on the fsbo_* FIELDS but never on the fsbo_followups
TABLE, so a lead in the FSBO sequence whose fsbo_status had been cleared (an Off
Market listing clears it) could still auto-enrol. Closed.

An ordinary lead is unaffected - asserted, because a guard that quietly switches
the AI off for everyone would be its own outage.

entries.subject: Close the FSBO hole at the send gate too, and cover all three layers
entries.title: Close the FSBO hole at the send gate too, and cover all three layers
entries.body:
policy.js is the last gate before anything goes out. It denied Cancelled/Expired
and had nothing for FSBO, so that is where an AI text to a FSBO seller would still
have slipped through even with the two inbound guards.

It now denies on fsbo_followups AND on client.fsbo_status, the second catching a
seller the campaign table has not caught up with. Scoped to channel 'ai', so the
campaigns' own approved templates ('automation'/'drip') are untouched - blocking
too broadly would have silenced the FSBO campaign itself.

Why a send-time check is needed at all: AI enrolment already excludes an FSBO
lead, but only AT THE MOMENT OF ENROLMENT. A cold buyer later identified as a FSBO
seller stays AI-managed and the exclusion never fires again. That is how Joseph
Green and Jamie Northrup were reachable - both are typed 'buyer'.

Audited: 2 breaches, both FSBO. Leeann Jones also had an AI text but it predates
her Cancelled/Expired enrolment by two weeks, so that guard has never failed.

entries.title: AI must never reply to an FSBO seller either

and Cancelled/Expired". On 2026-10-05 the AI answered Joseph Green about
7526 Cattail Ct NE - he replied "Yes, it is available." at 16:10 and the AI came
back with "How's it going so far with the sale?" one minute later.

  routes/inbox.js awaited handleCxInbound and used its answer to block the AI, but

  in depth for every other caller" - but only ever covered Cancelled/Expired. It

replied to, so the damage can be seen rather than guessed at.

entries.subject: Tasks tab: stop the automations writing to it
entries.title: Tasks tab: stop the automations writing to it
entries.body:
John: keep the Tasks tab for our own manual work, remove what AI added. 71 of 239
tasks had been written by automations - 42 CX Response, 17 FSBO Response, 11
Annual Not in Market Recheck, 1 Fix It or Skip It. Those 71 are deleted (a copy of
every one was taken first).

Deleting alone would have fixed nothing: a CX Response task is written every time a
cancelled/expired lead replies, so the tab refills within days. Creation is now
gated behind automation_tasks_enabled, default OFF - a setting rather than deleted
code, so it can be turned back on without a release.

Nothing is lost by it. Every gated path already raises a notification at the
moment it matters ("RESPONSE RECEIVED - <name>"), and the conversation is in the
Inbox either way. The task was a second copy of a signal that already existed.

THE ANNUAL NOT IN MARKET RECHECK IS THE EXCEPTION, and is restored, both the code
and the 11 rows. It is not noise that regenerates - it is one human to-do a YEAR
out, and it is load-bearing: followup-coverage.js counts a future human task as
the coverage for a parked lead ("the annual recheck task IS the coverage"). Remove
it and every Not in Market lead evaluates UNPROTECTED and lands in Needs
Attention, trading one kind of clutter for another. notify() cannot stand in: it
fires immediately and cannot be scheduled a year ahead.

Matching for the purge was by the exact title templates in the code, never by
category: 'follow-up' is also a category a person can pick, and 10 client-linked
tasks are plainly hand-written ("Let's do a follow up for Rose...", bare names).
Deleting by category would have taken those too.

entries.subject: The never-lose rule turned on vagueness; it should turn on authority
entries.title: The never-lose rule turned on vagueness; it should turn on authority
entries.body:
A live run wrote 130 updates and 17 of them lost information, all reverted:

  13  High Probability Sellers -> High Probability Buyer   (from the Hub's `type`)
   2  PLATINUM CLIENTS         -> High Probability Buyer
   2  Past Client              -> ACTIVE WITH AGENT

The rule only blocked a VAGUE target landing on a specific stage. A target that
was merely DIFFERENT went straight through, so a one-word Hub status was allowed
to overwrite a better-sourced FUB stage. I had flagged the seller-to-buyer risk
on 10-01 and then ran the push without resolving it, which is how it reached
production.

The test is no longer "is the target vague" but "does the Hub actually KNOW
better":

  authoritative - mls_status says Expired or Cancelled, or the lead is Junk/DNC
                  and must stop looking workable. These may still overwrite.
  derived       - anything computed from the coarse status or type field. These
                  never overwrite a specific stage.

So junk still clears High Probability Sellers, which John asked for, and
mls_status still upgrades a Watch into Expired, which adds information. What can
no longer happen is `type` flipping a seller to a buyer, or an active status
erasing a past client.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Junk must not sit on a workable FUB stage
entries.title: Junk must not sit on a workable FUB stage
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-05: "make sure that there's nothing in Junk from HUB that is still
on active stage in FUB, they must be on Dead Stage".

Nurture, Seller (NURTURE) and the High Probability pair all read as WORKABLE in
FUB - an agent opening one of those expects to work it - so the demotion guard
was too broad in holding them back. A lead the Hub has marked Junk now clears
them.

What stays protected is only what is genuinely historical or curated: Past
Client, Closed, Under Contract and PLATINUM CLIENTS. Junk on one of those is far
more likely to be a mistake in the Hub than a reason to erase the history, so it
is still reported for a person rather than written.

The guard remains scoped to demotions, so parity moves are untouched by it.

entries.subject: FUB sync adds information, never loses it
entries.title: FUB sync adds information, never loses it
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-05: leave a lead's stage alone where the push would flatten it, and
send the Hub's expired/cancelled listings to FUB's own Expired and Cancelled
stages instead of the generic Watch.

A full dry walk of 2,935 moves found 154 that would have replaced a SPECIFIC FUB
stage with 'Watch': 45 PLATINUM CLIENTS, 56 Cancelled, 53 Expired. The Hub's
vaguest status overwriting FUB's most precise.

Two changes:

1. stageFor() now reads what the Hub KNOWS before its coarse status field. An
   expired listing is 'watch' in the Hub because that is the only word the status
   vocabulary has, but mls_status says exactly what it is and FUB has a stage for
   it. Watch -> Expired ADDS information; Watch -> Watch would have thrown it
   away. Only expired and cancelled are mapped; Active and Pending are left
   rather than guessed.

2. wouldLoseInformation() refuses any write that puts a vague stage on top of a
   specific one, and reports it as 'kept-specific' with the reason. That covers
   PLATINUM CLIENTS, Cancelled, Expired, Foreclosures, Probates, Past Client,
   Under Contract and the High Probability pair - anything the Hub's status
   cannot reconstruct.

The cleanup that was the point of the exercise still runs: 268 Nurture and 231
Seller (NURTURE) still become Watch, because vague-to-vague loses nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

property these days?" - too direct and a bit out of touch. Asking an owner whose
listing just expired what their plans are, offering nothing and acknowledging

Removed from ANGLES and from ROTATION. The body is composed at send time rather
than queued ahead, so nothing was sitting in a queue carrying this wording and

and every age bucket still has well above the 3-send no-repeat window.

ROTATION is now exported so a test can hold the invariant that bit here: a key
listed in ROTATION but missing from ANGLES throws at ANGLES[angle].text(), during

entries.subject: A lead added by hand never auto-enrolls in AI, unless it is turned on
entries.title: A lead added by hand never auto-enrolls in AI, unless it is turned on
entries.body:
Holly Stock was added in the Hub at 15:38 and got an AI intro text at 15:46, 22
seconds before a real human group message to her and Matt about her mother's
condo. She read as a generic prospect and a known seller inside half a minute.

The status check did not save her. This route defaults a lead to 'active', but
the fresh-lane hook runs the instant the row exists, so a lead typed in as New,
or left New for the seconds before the status is set, is eligible.

So the exclusion is recorded on the record at creation rather than inferred from
status, using the SAME durable flag an agent sets from the profile. That is what
makes "unless turned on" work already: POST /api/ai/lead/:id/enable does not
consult the flag, so switching AI on by hand still does exactly what it says.

The enrolment hook still runs, so the decision is evaluated and logged rather
than skipped in silence - the decision log is the record of why nothing fired.
Marking the exclusion is best-effort and wrapped, because failing to set a guard
must never stop a lead being created.

entries.title: Run the new-lead push hourly, shipped OFF
entries.body:
"Moving forward" means it has to run by itself, so an hourly tick sweeps the Hub
leads FUB does not know about.

A sweep rather than a hook on each insert: leads are created from eight different
places in this codebase, and one sweep catches all of them without eight hooks to
keep in step. Batches of 25, because each lead costs up to two FUB searches at
260ms pacing.

Forward-only by construction - pushNewLeads stamps its cutoff on the first run,
so the tick can never wake up and backfill the ~14,000 older unlinked leads.

Gated behind fub_push_new_enabled, default '0', like every other automation here.

entries.subject: New Hub leads are pushed into FUB
entries.title: New Hub leads are pushed into FUB
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-01: "when someone is added in HUB make sure they are also pushed in
FUB".

SEARCH BEFORE CREATE. FUB can be searched by email and by phone, and both return
the exact person - verified against a lead known to be in both systems. So a lead
FUB already has is LINKED (its fub_person_id written back), and only someone FUB
genuinely does not know is created. That is safer than trusting FUB's own dedupe
semantics, which we have not verified.

A lead with neither an email nor a phone is SKIPPED, not created: that is the one
case that could genuinely duplicate in FUB, and the record would be useless there
anyway.

"Moving forward" is taken literally. The cutoff is stamped on the first run and
stored, so this never backfills the ~14,000 older unlinked leads by surprise.

New records are created with the parity stage from stageFor(), falling back to
'Lead' when the status is unmapped - 'new' is deliberately absent from the
mapping, but a brand-new FUB record still needs somewhere to land.

fubPost no longer refuses /people. That guard was mine, written hours earlier,
and it stood for the wrong invariant: the rule has always been about DIRECTION.
Nothing is pulled FROM FUB into the Hub, because that is what makes Hub
duplicates. Pushing a Hub lead INTO FUB is the opposite, and the Hub is master.

Paced and resumable like every other push. Nothing is scheduled yet.

entries.title: HUB -> FUB status parity, so the two systems read the same
entries.body:
John found Mark McDermott showing Prime in the Hub and Seller (NURTURE) in FUB,
and asked for them to match (2026-10-01).

The mapping is not guesswork. I sampled where these people already sit in FUB
before writing any of it:

  closed        -> Past Client        11 of 12 already there
  pending       -> Under Contract     1 of 1
  active        -> ACTIVE WITH AGENT  5 of 10, FUB's own word for a working lead
  not_in_market -> Not in the Market
  watch         -> Watch              CREATED; FUB had no equivalent and those
                                      leads were spread across Nurture, Seller
                                      (NURTURE), Cancelled and six more
  prime         -> High Probability Buyer | Sellers, by the lead's type, because
                                      FUB already splits that one by who they are

'new' is deliberately NOT pushed. It is 28,676 people, about half of them staged
'Realist' in FUB, which records where the lead came from. The Hub's 'new' does
not carry that, so pushing would flatten ~20,000 records and lose the source for
good. John's call. 'qualify' and 'archived' are a couple of people each with no
clean equivalent, so they are left rather than misfiled.

The protected-stage guard now applies to DEMOTIONS only. Overwriting a meaningful
stage is the point of parity; dropping a Past Client to Dead is not, so Dead and
Do not Contact keep the protection.

fubPost exists now, for stages only - it refuses /people outright, because
pulling leads out of FUB is what would create duplicates.

entries.subject: FUB conversations: import for Active leads first
entries.title: FUB conversations: import for Active leads first
entries.body:
Starts where it is most useful and least risky: status='active' is 42 linked
leads, the ones the team is actually working (John, 2026-10-01). A scoped run
cannot wander into the 264k-note history.

Everything is fetched per personId, including notes and calls, which can be
pulled in bulk. One shape for all three channels, and it only ever touches the
leads asked for. Bulk is the right tool for a full historical backfill, not a
scoped run.

  - lands in `communications`, which already feeds the Inbox and the profile
  - external_id is namespaced per channel (fub_note_/fub_call_/fub_text_) and
    UNIQUE, so a re-run adds nothing twice
  - rows the Hub itself wrote into FUB are skipped on the way back, via the
    systemName the X-System header stamps, so a two-way sync cannot ping-pong
  - note bodies are stripped to text and capped; 2.4 KB of Sierra email HTML
    becomes a readable line, which is what makes the import affordable when ten
    retained backups multiply every megabyte
  - undated rows are dropped rather than sorting to the top of a timeline
  - paced at 260ms on every call including the error path, because FUB rate-limits
  - the disk is re-checked DURING the run, not once at the start, and the run
    stops itself below the floor
  - resumable by afterId

POST /api/fub/import-conversations takes {dry:true} first. Nothing is scheduled.

entries.subject: FSBO: stop collapsing Disregard and Sold into Off Market
entries.title: FSBO: stop collapsing Disregard and Sold into Off Market
entries.body:
Recognising the statuses was not enough. The per-seller aggregate - the line that
actually writes fsbo_status - read:

  Available ? 'Available' : Pending ? 'Pending' : 'Off Market'

so every value that was not Available or Pending became Off Market. normStatus
had Disregard and Sold right; this line threw the answer away, which is why they
reached the Hub as Off Market, stayed on the list, and were never junked.

Found by measuring rather than reasoning: a read-only diagnostic inside the
deployed process showed the sheet parsed as Disregard=7, Sold=3 while the sync
reported Off Market=35 (25+7+3). Same process, same URL, so the loss had to be
between the two.

Available still wins - a seller with one listing sold and another still for sale
is a live FSBO. Otherwise the group's own ending survives.

entries.subject: FSBO: Sold and Disregard end the lead, same as Pending
entries.title: FSBO: Sold and Disregard end the lead, same as Pending
entries.body:
The master file carries five FSBO Status values, not three. Sold and Disregard
fell through normStatus to null, and a null status makes the sync SKIP the row -
which is not the same as removing it. The skipped rows kept whatever status the
Hub had last written, so four of the seven Disregard sellers were still live on
the FSBO list, frozen at the "Off Market" they held before the sheet changed.

Disregard means they listed with an agent (John, 2026-10-01). Sold means it sold.
Both are finished, so both now junk like Pending, stop every sequence, and keep
fsbo_status as the record of WHICH ending it was. The profile log names the
reason rather than the lead just going quiet.

Off Market still does NOT junk. Those sellers tried and failed to sell alone,
which makes them a better prospect, not a worse one.

Also fixed in the multi-listing aggregation: with no Available listing it fell
back to 'Off Market', which could relabel a seller who had sold, or listed with
an agent, and leave them on the list. It now prefers an ending the group actually
carries.

entries.subject: Assessor button: resolve the parcel on the server, and link to it
entries.title: Assessor button: resolve the parcel on the server, and link to it
entries.body:
John: the button "doesn't get any result". It didn't, and nor did the version
before it. Both tried to do this with a URL, and there is no URL that takes an
address and lands on a parcel:

  results.php?ifulladdress=...&process=1  is not a page on either site. It lands
    on an empty Residential Building Search. That is what shipped until now.
  /search/res/results/?ifulladdress=...   replays whatever the session last
    POSTed - four different addresses once returned the same parcel.
  /search/res/                            shows the PREVIOUS search, which is how
    6528 Medford Ln NE appeared on Adrien Voellinger's profile.

A browser cannot do it because the disclaimer cookie VCSID is SameSite=Lax, so it
is not sent on a cross-site POST, and the search is a POST. A server has no such
rule. server/assessor-lookup.js does the whole flow with a cookie jar: collect the
cookie, accept the disclaimer (search_disclaimer=1 + i_agree), then replay the
search form WITH ITS OWN HIDDEN FIELDS - sending ifulladdress alone bounces
straight back - and follow the 303 to /parcel/<hash>.

Both hosts are tried. A Cedar Rapids postal address can sit outside the city
limits and belong to the county assessor: 3 of the 9 that resolved only did so
after that fallback.

A parcel is only accepted when its own Property Address matches the one searched,
the same safety rule as the Forewarn lookup - linking a stranger's property is
worse than linking nothing. The site writes "ST" out as "STREET", so both sides
are expanded before comparing.

Verified against 10 real client addresses: 9 resolved, every one showing the
address asked for, 9 distinct parcels. The 10th is in Anamosa, which is Jones
County and genuinely not on either site.

The result is cached on the client (a parcel does not move); a miss is retried
after a week. The button resolves when the profile opens, so the real link is
already in it by the time it is clicked, and assessorUrl is now only the fallback
for an address with no record.

Two bugs the new tests caught before this shipped: the <select> default picked the
first option whenever `selected` came after `value`, and streetOnly left "Unit"
behind on "190 Cottage Grove Ave SE Unit #302".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Put the full-row button rule in a narrow query, not the desktop one
entries.title: Put the full-row button rule in a narrow query, not the desktop one
entries.body:
The rule that makes the actions take their own row went into
@media (min-width: 901px) - the DESKTOP block - so it forced them off the name's
line at exactly the widths where they were meant to sit beside it. The computed
style gave it away: flex 1 1 100% and margin-top 6px at 1500px wide, while the
rule meant for that width said 1 1 320px. My comment called it "on a phone",
which it never was.

entries.subject: Hub phone: retry setup instead of giving up after one try
entries.title: Hub phone: retry setup instead of giving up after one try
entries.body:
John hit "The Hub phone is not connected yet". The server was fine - I checked
/api/voice/token while the toast was showing and it returned a valid JWT,
identity hub, incoming allowed, outgoing app SID, an hour of life left. The CDN
and Twilio were reachable too.

The fault was that setup ran exactly once. init() was called bare in the effect
with nothing watching for failure, so any single hiccup left deviceRef null and
the phone dead until someone reloaded the page by hand. The likeliest hiccup is a
deploy, which is what happened repeatedly today: Render restarts, the token
endpoint answers with an HTML error page, r.json() throws, and the phone never
comes back even though the server is healthy seconds later. Same root cause as
the hard-refresh problem in this file's header.

  - ensureDevice() runs one attempt at a time and shares it with every caller
  - failures back off 2s, 4s, 8s, 15s then every 30s, and keep trying
  - returning to the tab or regaining the network retries at once and resets the
    backoff
  - a Device that fails to register is destroyed and nulled, so a half-built one
    is never mistaken for a working phone
  - pressing Call now connects on demand and only falls back to the toast, which
    says it is retrying and why
  - the reason comes from a ref; the effect runs once with [], so a captured
    regErr would have stayed empty forever

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Groundwork for the FUB conversation sync (not yet wired up)
entries.title: Groundwork for the FUB conversation sync (not yet wired up)
entries.body:
Mappers and helpers only - nothing calls this module yet, so the deploy is inert
and tomorrow starts from a known place.

What the probes established against the live FUB account:

  notes    264,069  full body        bulk + incremental via updatedAfter
  calls     38,280  outcome/duration bulk + incremental
  texts    per person, full message  NO bulk, personId is required
  emails   per person, CONTENT HIDDEN

Emails cannot be synced. FUB returns "[CONTENT HIDDEN]" for every subject and
body - 51 of 51 sampled across three people. Metadata only, and not a permission
we can change from our side.

Note bodies are stripped to text. Measured 2.4 KB of HTML each, almost all Sierra
Interactive email copies, so 609 MB across 264k rows. The volume is 9.8 GB with
7.4 GB free, which would fit, except 10 backup copies of the database are retained
and that multiplies every megabyte of growth by ten - the same shape as the
2026-09-21 disk-full incident. Stripping keeps every note and every word at
roughly 0.5 KB.

The loop breaker is already in place: FUB stamps systemName from the X-System
header and fub-helper sends MattSmithTeamHub, so a two-way sync skips the Hub's
own writes rather than ping-ponging.

Everything lands in `communications`, which already feeds both the Inbox and the
profile timeline, and whose external_id is UNIQUE so a re-run is harmless.

entries.subject: Client profile: assessor and FUB buttons, and push Hub status to FUB
entries.title: Client profile: assessor and FUB buttons, and push Hub status to FUB
entries.body:
THREE THINGS.

1. Assessor button. Cedar Rapids has its OWN city assessor; Linn County covers everywhere
   else - Marion, Hiawatha, Robins, Ely. Sending a Cedar Rapids address to the county site
   finds nothing, and most of the file is Cedar Rapids, so routing by city is not an
   optimisation. It opens the assessor's SEARCH with the address filled in, not the parcel
   page: both sites gate on a disclaimer cookie and search by POST, so no URL takes an
   address and lands on a parcel. A resolver that stores each parcel id would make this a
   true deep link; until then this is one click away and does not break when they redesign.

2. View FUB Profile button, for the 31,868 leads that have a fub_person_id. Hidden for the
   rest rather than linking somewhere that 404s.

3. Hub status pushed to FUB, ONE DIRECTION. A lead marked Junk here should not sit in FUB
   as New where an agent works someone already disqualified.

     Hub Junk          ->  FUB "Dead"            (15,919 already there)
     Hub DoNotContact  ->  FUB "Do not Contact"  (285)

   Both stages already existed, so nothing new is invented. The other Hub statuses are
   deliberately unmapped: New, Prime, Watch and the rest have no FUB equivalent and
   guessing at one would mean guessing how the team uses their pipeline.

   Nothing is ever pulled FROM FUB - that is what would create duplicates. The only FUB
   data entering the Hub stays the Facebook ad-lead emails, which already dedupe on phone
   then email before inserting.

   The write path is deliberately narrow: update one person by id. No bulk, no create, no
   delete. A person missing from FUB is reported, never created. Tags are MERGED, because
   FUB replaces the tag array on a PUT and sending only the new tag would wipe the rest.
   Paced at 220ms because this is a live CRM.

POST /api/fub/push-statuses takes {dry:true}. Nothing has been pushed yet.
